name: Slow Cooker BBQ Pulled Chicken Bowls
intro_html: This is the kind of meal that makes the whole week easier. You get tender BBQ pulled chicken over rice with a hit of sweet corn, {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, and it lands right around ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost). Fourteen servings out of one pot means lunch is handled before Monday even starts.
ingredients_display: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 8 lb (3300 g)
BBQ Sauce (Sugar Free) (Sweet Baby Ray's): 1 3/4 cups (500 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 4 1/2 cups (750 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast, 8 lb: ~$16.22. Buy 8 lbs: $17.84.
Rice, 5.25 cups dry: ~$1.17. Pantry staple; this batch alone uses about 2 2lb bags.
BBQ Sauce (Sugar Free), 1 3/4 cups: ~$3.07. Buy 1 (covers this batch).
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn, 4 1/2 cups: ~$1.06. Buy 2 cans: $1.22.
Pantry seasonings (paprika, garlic powder, salt, black pepper): ~$0.46. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $21.98 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.57 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $23.76 across 14 servings, roughly $1.70 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $6.68 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $30.44. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
shop_smart: Buy the chicken breast in an 8 lb bulk pack instead of small trays. You are already cooking a big batch, so the per-pound price drops and you skip a second trip.
Grab a sugar-free BBQ sauce to keep the carbs and calories in check without giving up the flavor that carries this whole bowl.
Canned corn on sale beats fresh here. Watch for the store brand under 70 cents a can and stock a few.
make_it: Lay the chicken breasts in the bottom of the slow cooker.
Sprinkle the paprika, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper over the top, then pour on the BBQ sauce.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the chicken shreds with a fork.
Shred the chicken right in the pot and stir it back through the sauce.
Warm the corn and fold it in, or spoon it over the top.
Serve over cooked white rice and portion into your containers.
portion_html: Each of the 14 servings runs about {{cal}} calories with a serious {{protein}} grams of protein.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from Budget Bytes, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.
upsell_html: Make it once and you will wonder why you ever paid for fast food lunches. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
